plans.note: Para 21.3 (p0242-p0245) is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential loss and lost profits covering delay, failure of APCN 2 and service interruption; para 4.9 (p0126) exculpates PG members for Supplier failure. Mutuality is satisfied; there is no aggregate monetary cap and no express carve-outs (e.g. wilful misconduct, confidentiality, third-party indemnity) — note the missing cap/carve-out mechanics in the rationale rather than treating symmetric exclusions as a deviation. Cross-check against the pro-rata third-party indemnity in p0241 before concluding.

Indemnity architecture exists but is consortium-style and mutual: para 21.2 (p0241) has each Party indemnify the others for third-party claims arising from APCN 2 ownership, capped at that Party's Schedule B share; Paragraph 32 (p0275-p0280) is a reimbursement/claims-handling regime in Schedule B proportions, with claim-conduct control vested in the Management Committee (p0276-p0278) and survival after termination (p0280). No vendor-side IP infringement or misconduct indemnity flows to us alone — note this gap, not a blanket 'missing' finding.

No restrictive covenant located. All 'compete' hits are 'competent jurisdiction'/'competent tribunal' (p0272, p0275). Nothing restricts the businesses we may operate or the systems we may build or buy; no comment needed.

No supply exclusivity. The only 'exclusive' hit is p0262, the 'sole and exclusive remedy' language in the dispute procedure (address under GOVLAW, not here). Paras 17.2-17.4 (p0225-p0227) affirmatively require reasonable, non-discriminatory access and forbid impeding Direct Access, which favours us.

No MFN/most-favoured-customer clause anywhere; searches for 'most favoured/favored' and 'more favourable' returned nothing. The nearest concept is the 'reasonable and non-discriminatory' arrangements duty on Terminal Parties (p0225-p0226), which runs in our favour. No burden on us to extend best terms.
No non-solicitation or no-hire covenant located; searches for solicit/hire/employ returned no hits. Nothing to redline.

Paragraph 18 governs exit. Para 18.1 (p0228) locks all Parties in for a 25-year Initial Period, with unilateral withdrawal only at or after the end of that period on 1 year's written notice; during the Initial Period termination requires unanimous written agreement or a 90% Management Committee majority (p0229). Para 18.3 (p0230) sets a 66.67% decommissioning threshold and para 18.5/18.7 (p0232, p0235) impose continuing obligations; p0233 denies any capital-cost credit to a withdrawing Party. Assess whether no-convenience-exit for 25 years plus forfeiture of capital contribution clears the fallback; the forfeiture element is also picked up under LD, so avoid double-flagging the same money term.

No auto-renewal mechanic: para 18.1 (p0228) runs for an initial 25-year period from the RFS Date and is 'terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties', i.e. it continues indefinitely by default rather than renewing in fixed terms, with 1 year's notice to withdraw. There is no renewal pricing uplift and no non-renewal notice window to negotiate; p0042 confirms the MOU continued only until signature of this Agreement. Note the evergreen-continuation structure and the 1-year notice length; there is no renewal price-escalation risk to cap.

Material deviation candidate. Para 27.2 (p0263) deliberately refuses to designate a governing law and directs courts and tribunals to disregard the facts that would identify one; para 27.1 (p0262) makes referral to the Management Committee, which may itself choose the method such as arbitration, the 'sole and exclusive remedy' for all disputes, so we have no court recourse. Para 20 (p0239) presupposes arbitration in an unspecified foreign seat, and para 25 (p0260) only promises compliance with all applicable local laws. None of New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales is selected and no venue/seat is fixed.

Para 22.1 (p0246) is a general no-assignment rule, but 22.2 permits whole transfers with Management Committee consent that 'must not [be] unreasonably withhold[ing] or delay[ed]', and 22.3 (p0247-p0250) permits assignment without consent to a successor, Parent Company, Subsidiary or Affiliate — which meets our affiliate/successor position. Note the limits: partial assignments to affiliates are allowed only once per Assignee and do not release the Assignor (p0251), territorial assignments carry conditions (p0252-p0253), and notice to all Parties is required (p0254). Successors are bound (p0269). No change-of-control termination right runs against us.

Ownership is asset-based, not IP-based: para 4.3 (p0119) fixes Wet Segment ownership per Schedule B, para 4.1 (p0107) allocates Segment ownership, and para 12.2 (p0187) confirms Parties obtain Allocated Capacity on an ownership basis in return for their investment, with Schedule revisions on transfer (p0210, p0214). IRU is defined as conveying no ownership (p0054). There is no deliverables/work-product or customer-data ownership clause; confidentiality (p0270) is the only data protection, and it vests disclosure control in the Management Committee. Note that we own what we pay for at the capacity/segment level and that no IP or data is assigned away from us.

The licence analogue is the IRU regime: p0054/p0049 define IRU as an Indefeasible Right of Use (i.e. not revocable at will, which satisfies our core concern), p0202 sets MIU-level sales from Unallocated Capacity, and p0209 defers IRU terms and conditions to guidelines to be developed by the subcommittee — the operative scope is therefore not yet fixed in this document. Affiliate and contractor use is not addressed in the grant itself; affiliate transfer is handled by para 22.3-22.5 (p0247-p0252). Note the deferred terms and the absence of express affiliate/contractor use rights.

Paragraph 9 is a mutual books-and-records regime (5-year retention, p0160-p0166) giving any Party the right to review or audit (p0167). It runs to our benefit as much as against us, but note two burdens: under 9.8 (p0167) the audited Party recovers its entire compliance costs from the requesting Party (so our own audits are at our cost, contrary to our vendor-cost position), and under 9.9 (p0168) audit rights are exercisable only through the F&ASC per its procedures. There is no notice period, frequency limit or off-site preference — note these mechanics.

Deviation candidate on penalty exposure running against us. Para 23.1-23.2 (p0255-p0256) allows the Management Committee to reclaim our allocated capacity for payment default after notice, with no payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity, forfeiture of amounts already paid, loss of Party status, and continuing liability for accrued unpaid accounts; a Terminal Party must still operate its Terminal Station (p0257). Default interest accrues at a prime/minimum commercial lending rate (p0153) and p0233 denies capital-cost credit on withdrawal. Frame the forfeiture-without-credit as the penalty issue here and cross-reference, do not re-flag, the exit timing raised under T4C. No service credits run to us.

Deviation candidate. Para 4.9 (p0126-p0127) is an express disclaimer: the PG makes no representations or warranties as to Supplier performance under the Supply Contract, the performance or reliability of the Wet Segment, or that APCN 2 will be integrated or placed into operation, and nothing in the Agreement is to be construed as such a warranty. The only remedy pathway is the PG's discretionary exercise of Supply Contract rights, subject to Management Committee direction (p0124-p0125), which is not a warranty remedy running to us. No warranty period and no conformity-to-specification commitment.

No mandatory insurance covenant. Para 5.3 (p0139) makes insurance purely optional — each Party 'may at its own expense insure against risks' for its own share, and joint insurance becomes a Capital Cost only if the Parties agree; O&M cost definitions treat insurance or an allowance in lieu as a recoverable cost item (p0133, p0141-p0142), and construction-phase damage is simply absorbed into Capital Costs (p0138). No minimum limits, no certificate, additional-insured or waiver-of-subrogation mechanics. Treat as effectively absent for our purposes and note the cost-sharing consequence of an uninsured loss.

There is no take-or-pay purchase commitment in the vendor sense, but there are open-ended cost-sharing obligations: Capital Costs and O&M Costs are allocated by Schedule B investment shares (p0128, p0040), capacity is obtained in Minimum Investment Units (p0055, p0187), and upgrades of Equipped Capacity under para 13.1 (p0215) carry cost and financial consequences that should be checked for whether our share can be increased without our consent. Non-payment triggers interest (p0153) and capacity reclamation (see LD). Confirm the Paragraph 13 voting/consent mechanics before concluding; note the absence of any cap on incremental contributions.

Only partial, asset-side transition provisions exist: on withdrawal or capacity reclamation the Parties must negotiate a reasonable agreement to ensure continuous operation of the relevant Terminal Station (p0231, p0257), remaining Parties assume the departing Party's interests and obligations (p0232), and decommissioning/liquidation is addressed in p0234. Confidentiality survives 5 years (p0274) and records are retained for 5 years (p0166), with post-termination third-party liabilities shared per Schedule B (p0280). There is no data-return, no migration or termination-assistance obligation and no defined transition period — note the gap rather than claiming nothing exists.
